name: ButtonGroup
statusNote: ButtonGroup is a thin layout wrapper around Button and IconButton and ships widely; alpha is Primer's label. Its CSS still carries a workaround for portal-based tooltips and a loading-button rule that, as written, does not match (see notes).
summary: Joins related Buttons and IconButtons into one segmented strip whose borders touch. Choose it for a split button or a cluster of peer actions; choose ActionBar when the row must collapse into an overflow menu, and SegmentedControl when exactly one option is selected.

inputs.name: children
inputs.description: The buttons, in order: Button, IconButton or LinkButton, any variant, normally all the same size and variant.

inputs.name: role
inputs.description: Set to toolbar to turn on arrow-key navigation between the buttons; any other value (or none) leaves each button a separate Tab stop.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Names the group; needed when role is toolbar.

anatomy.name: Group
anatomy.description: An inline row with no gap and no styling of its own; it creates a stacking context so raised children never escape it.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: A wrapper around each child; it pulls the next item 1px left so adjacent borders overlap into a single line, and rises above its neighbours while hovered or pressed.

anatomy.name: Button
anatomy.description: The child Button or IconButton, unchanged except for its corner radii: square inside the group, --borderRadius-medium on the outer corners of the first and last.

variants.description: No role: a visual grouping only; each button is its own Tab stop.
role=toolbar: arrow keys move focus between the buttons and wrap at the ends.

layout.text: Lay the children out in one row with no gap; the group is inline and vertically centred on the surrounding text.

Every item but the last overlaps the next by 1px (a -1px end margin), so two 1px borders draw as one; the group is 1px narrower per joint than the sum of its buttons. The last item also carries the -1px margin, so the group's box ends 1px inside its last button.
Square every child's corners, then round the start corners of the first item and the end corners of the last item with --borderRadius-medium. A group of one button keeps all four corners round.
Each child is wrapped in its own item box in order, so the corner rules depend on the wrapper's position, not on the button inside it.

states.text: Raise the hovered item above its neighbours (z-index 1) so its hover border colour paints over the shared 1px edge instead of under it.
Raise the pressed item the same way, so its active border shows on both edges.
The focused button draws its own inset focus outline (Button's rule); the group adds nothing, and because the outline sits 2px inside the border, the 1px overlap never hides it.

behaviour.text: With role toolbar, Left and Right arrows move focus between the buttons and wrap from last to first; with no role the group binds no keys.
Each child keeps its own variant, size, loading and disabled behaviour; the group does not propagate size or variant, so the caller must keep them consistent.

accessibility.role: none by default; toolbar when role is toolbar (each child keeps role button)
keyboard: Without role toolbar: Tab moves through the buttons one by one.
With role toolbar: Left and Right arrows move between buttons, wrapping at the ends.
semantics: The group itself is announced only when it has a role; a toolbar needs an accessible name from ariaLabel.
Each button keeps its own name and state.

notes.text: The rules for a loading button's wrapper (selector > *[data-loading-wrapper]) target a direct child of the group, but ButtonGroup wraps every child in an .Item div, so the loading wrapper is never a direct child and those rules never apply. The .Item rules already square and round the inner button, so a native build can ignore the loading branch.

A child that renders nothing still gets an .Item wrapper, which takes a -1px margin and, if it is last, steals the last-item rounding. The group answers with a :has(div:last-child:empty) rule that rounds every button fully, which also rounds the inner joints. A native build should drop empty children before layout rather than copy this.
The raise rule lists :focus on the .Item div, which never takes focus itself; focus does not raise an item. Only hover and press do.

Arrow navigation comes from useFocusZone in @primer/behaviors, which is not vendored. It conventionally makes the toolbar one Tab stop with a roving tabindex; treat that as expected but unverified here.
Overlap and stacking come from negative margins, isolation and z-index; a native build draws the buttons in order with the hovered or pressed one last, and shares one border line at each joint.
